newsitem.title: UK: Sterling robust, scores fresh 52-mth highs vs mark.
newsitem.headline: Sterling robust, scores fresh 52-mth highs vs mark.

text.p: Sterling climbed to new 52-month peaks of 2.7460 marks in late Europe on Tuesday and analysts say further gains are expected as a strong UK economy highlights German economic weakness.
"The UK economy is doing well. The currency is also an EMU (European monetary union) "safe haven"," said Lee Ferridge, currency strategist at Commerzbank.
At 1511 GMT sterling was trading at 2.7430/40 marks, just off fresh 52-month peaks of 2.7460 marks but some three pfennigs up from 2.7130/40 in late Europe on Monday.
Against the dollar, sterling was also a touch firmer.
At 1517 GMT, sterling was trading at $1.6436/46 against $1.6380/90 in late Europe on Monday.

Traders said sterling got a fresh shot in the arm on Tuesday from dollar/mark strength, a Times newspaper column - a reminder of German economic weakness - and a BBC report saying rising German unemployment had pushed expectations for a 1997 budget deficit to 3.5 percent of GDP.
"The German economy is in very poor shape - that is not news - but we have seen a couple of high profile stories highlighting the problems," said David Coleman, chief economist at CIBC Wood Gundy.
"We could well have a situation were we could end up at the old ERM (Exchange rate mechanism) 2.7780-mark level," he added.
Coleman said sterling is a good bet because it is likely to remain outside the first stage of European monetary union and the fact that the UK's economic fundamentals are looking good.
"The UK economy is growing quite well compared to the rest of Europe and Japan...And it's still very much a high-yielder," he said.
Even Prime Minister John Major had a part to play in sterling's rally on Tuesday, said analysts.

Britain's economy is more competitive than it has been in a long time despite sterling's recent rise, Major said. He described Britain's economic prospects as "sparklingly positive". Inflation was low, growth was rising, unemployment was falling, exports were rising and Britain was enjoying a degree of competitiveness, notwithstanding the recent rise in the exchange value of sterling against the deutschmark.
"Major's comments seem to have given the market a green light for further gains on Tuesday. The UK economy is doing well," said Commerzbank's Ferridge.
And even with interest not expected to rise this side of a general election, analysts said sterling should remain the darling of currency markets.
"Interest rates, while they have not gone up, are much higher than in Germany. Gilts are overperforming bunds and there is no stopping sterling," said Ferridge.
Even, said analysts, if UK unemployment figures due out on Wednesday are poor.
"Whatever the figures are, sterling will go up. Strong figures, a drop in unemployment, means rates will go up," said Coleman.
Coleman said a weak figure would encourage the gilt market to perform strongly and in turn send sterling higher.

UK January unemployment is expected to drop by 30,000 against a drop of 45,000 in December, that compares to Germany's unemployment rate which in January leaped by half a million to a post-war record of 4.66 million.
"The market is still factoring in Germany's huge jump in unemployment figures," said a senior trader at a German Bank.
--Julia Meehan, London newsroom +4471 542 6701
